why: Both match the key's hedgehog (cost-effective health-care portfolio, profit per employee, no big-pharma research race), refuse the merger/PBM wave and put the unresolved diagnostics quality findings first; Analysis 1 goes slightly further on early warnings by flagging joint-venture governance and decelerating, buyback-assisted earnings growth. Analysis 2 shows better restraint for an already-great company, framing the plan as temptations to refuse and preserving the portfolio, whereas Analysis 1 adds interventions such as a #1/#2 pruning review, walking away from price-only bids and halting diagnostics launches.
